persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Grace Miller, 45, the volunteer treasurer (the person who looks after the money) of Hope Valley Church in Austin, Texas, USA. In America, when someone gives money to a church, the church must send them a thank-you letter called a tax receipt, so the giver can pay less tax. Today you must get the church's details into the app and write the letters for three gifts.

lines: Welcome. This short video explains an app called Receipt Maker. You have never seen it, and that is fine. In about three minutes you will know what it is for and how to use it.
First, some background, because this is an American thing. In America, people who give money to a church or a charity can pay less tax.

But to do that, the giver needs a letter from the church. The letter must say how much they gave, the date, and some special words that the American tax office asks for. This letter is called a tax receipt.
A small church may have fifty or a hundred givers. Every January, a volunteer must write all those letters by hand. It can take a whole weekend, and it is easy to make mistakes.
Receipt Maker writes all the letters for you, in a few minutes, with the right words.
Who uses it? The treasurer or the secretary of a small church or charity. One person, on a phone or a computer.
The amounts are in dollars, because it is an American app. For this test, just type the numbers you are given.
Now let us walk through the page slowly. Everything is on one page, from top to bottom.
Section one is called Your organization. Organization means the church or charity. You fill this in once, and the phone remembers it.

lines.t: Organization name is the name of the church, as it should appear at the top of every letter.
EIN is the church's American tax number. It has nine digits, written like 12, dash, then seven more digits.
Address is the street, city and state. Signer is the person who signs the letters, with their job title, for example Grace Miller, Treasurer.
Section two is called The gifts. Each gift has its own row with three boxes: donor name, amount, and date received. A donor is the person who gave.

lines: In the amount box, type just the number, like 250. You do not need the dollar sign.

Sometimes a person gives a thing instead of money, for example a chair or a computer. This is called an in-kind gift. Then in the amount box you type the words in-kind, a colon, and what the thing was. For example: in-kind: used office desk.
The date box opens a calendar. Choose the day the gift came in.
To add another gift, tap the button Add another donor. To remove a row, tap the small cross at the end of the row.
If you have a long list, there is also a button called Paste a list instead. You do not need it today.

Under the gifts there are two tick boxes. Leave No goods or services ticked when the giver got nothing back. Tick We are a church if the organization is a church. The letter then uses special words for churches.

lines.t: Then tap the big gold button, Make the letters. The app writes one letter for each gift, and tells you if it skipped any row, and why.

lines: You can tap any letter to change its words. Then Print them all prints each letter on its own page.
Your church details and your gifts stay saved on this phone. The letters themselves are made fresh each time.
To start again with empty boxes, scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap Start fresh. It asks you twice.
In the test, you will be a church treasurer in America. Take your time. If anything is confusing, say so.

challenge.intro: Now you are Grace, the treasurer of Hope Valley Church. The app is empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press. Use what you learned. When you finish, tap Check my work. Dates: use the little 📅 calendar in the date box to pick the day. If you type it, look at the box first: many computers want the MONTH first (03/15/2026 = 15 March). Typing 15/03/2026 there gives the wrong date. After, check the box really shows the day you meant.
challenge.start: Use the NORMAL app link (not the 🧪 test copy). Open Receipt Maker. If the welcome tour shows, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own'. Then scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK. (If it says 'There is nothing saved in this app yet', tap OK: it is already empty.) All the boxes are now empty and there is one empty gift row. (Verified 10 Oct: all five checks false after this.)

tasks.text: Put in your church: Hope Valley Church, tax number (EIN) 74-1234567.
tasks.hint: Section 1, Your organization: the first two boxes.

tasks.text: The church is in Austin, Texas, and you, Grace Miller the Treasurer, sign the letters. Put that in.
tasks.hint: Section 1 also has an Address box and a Signer box. The signer needs a name AND a job title.

tasks.text: Mary Johnson gave $500 on 15 March 2026. Peter Brown gave $1,200 on 20 June 2026. Add both gifts.
tasks.hint: Section 2, The gifts: one row per gift, with name, amount and date. Use Add another donor for a second row. Check the amounts and the dates carefully. Dates: use the little 📅 calendar in the date box to pick the day. If you type it, look at the box first: many computers want the MONTH first (03/15/2026 = 15 March). Typing 15/03/2026 there gives the wrong date. After, check the box really shows the day you meant.

tasks.text: David Otieno gave the church a used laptop (no money) on 2 May 2026. Add this gift the right way.
tasks.hint: A gift of a thing, not money, is an in-kind gift. Remember how the video said to write it in the amount box. Dates: use the little 📅 calendar in the date box to pick the day. If you type it, look at the box first: many computers want the MONTH first (03/15/2026 = 15 March). Typing 15/03/2026 there gives the wrong date. After, check the box really shows the day you meant.

tasks.text: Your list must have exactly these three gifts and nothing else. Remove any other rows.
tasks.hint: Each row has a small × at its end to remove it.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: writes thank-you / tax receipt letters for people who gave to a church or charity
you type the organization once and one row per gift (name, amount, date)
makes all the letters at once with the right tax words, ready to print

daily.task: Make one new receipt in Receipt Maker for a made-up gift (a made-up name and amount). Don’t send or share it.

explore.name: 🏢 Section 1 · Your organization
explore.find: Open Receipt Maker. It is the top section.
explore.try: Fill name, EIN, address and signer. In EIN try letters, and only 5 numbers.

explore.name: 🎁 Section 2 · The gifts
explore.try: Fill three rows: a couple, a big amount like 1,200, and “in-kind”. Pick dates. Remove a row with ×. Tap ✚ Add another donor.

explore.name: 📋 Paste a list
explore.try: Paste three lines like “Mary Smith, 250, 2026-03-14”. Put these into the boxes. Then try one bad line.

explore.name: ☑️ The two tick boxes
explore.try: Untick “No goods or services” and tick “We are a church”. See the letters change.

explore.name: ✉️ Make the letters
explore.try: Make them with one row missing its amount — does it say which row it skipped and why?

explore.name: ✏️ Change a letter · 🖨 Print
explore.try: Change its words. Tap 🖨 Print them all (cancel the printer).

explore.name: ❓ The round ? button
explore.find: Tap the round ? in the bottom corner.
explore.try: Open every line in it: Aa (size), ✨ Ask an AI, 🌉 More from Daraja, 🎬 Take the tour again. Close it. Leave “Start fresh” for the very end.
